issues.failure_explanation: The proof expands u = Σ u^{(i)} e^{(i)} in the eigenbasis of the CLAMPED eigenproblem (eq:EVP), which is posed on H²∩H¹₀ and diagonalizes e(·,·) only on that space. For the sound-hard and impedance cases X = H²(Ω), which contains the constants, the expansion does not diagonalize the form: e(1,ζ) = 0 for all ζ, so P_W(1) = 0, T(1) = 1, and (AT1,1)_{H²} = e(1,1) − k²‖1‖²_{L²} = −k²|Ω| < 0, contradicting the claimed lower bound Re{a(Tu,u)} ≥ γ‖u‖²_X with γ > 0. Hence the theorem is false as stated for the spaces on which it is applied, and the weak T-coercivity framework (compact K plus injectivity) used for hard/impedance well-posedness collapses at its first step.

issues.overall_effect: The continuous well-posedness argument for sound-hard and impedance boundary conditions (and, via thm:vBZThm, the discrete impedance analysis and the best-approximation results thm:bestapprox/thm:added-3) loses its foundation; only the sound-soft case (X = H²∩H¹₀, K = 0) remains supported.

issues.failure_explanation: For u ∈ H²(Ω) one only has Δu ∈ L²(Ω) and 𝓗u ∈ L²(Ω); an L²(Ω) function has no L²(∂Ω) trace, so γ₀(Δu) and γ₀(nᵀ(𝓗u)n) are not defined, let alone continuous or compactly behaving, on X = H²(Ω). Hence the estimates ‖Ku‖_{H²} ≤ C‖γ₀Δu‖_{L²(∂Ω)} (and the nematic analogue) are meaningless, the sequence argument 'u_n ⇀ u in H² ⟹ Ku_n → Ku' cannot even be formulated, and the compactness of K — the keystone of the weak T-coercivity/Fredholm argument for hard and impedance conditions — is not established.

issues.failure_explanation: The theorem states self-adjointness for the nematic eigenproblem with no hypothesis on the director, but the proof assumes n = (n_x, n_y)ᵀ constant ('∇n is identically zero') and works in two dimensions. For a genuinely variable director field the form e(u,v) = \alpha(Δu,Δv) + \beta(nᵀ(𝓗u)n, Δv) + (∇u,∇v) is not symmetric (integration by parts of ∇·∇(nᵀ(𝓗u)n) produces \nabla n-terms), so the eigenvalues need not be real and the eigenfunctions need not form an orthogonal L² basis — the premise of the whole β > 0 construction (spectral sign-flipping operator T in eq:ToperatorBeta, thm:added-2) fails. The paper's own numerical examples use non-constant (piecewise discontinuous) directors, outside even the restricted setting.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypotheses actually used (∇n ≡ 0 and d = 2) to the statement, or supply the additional integration-by-parts terms that make the form symmetric for variable n; the spectral construction then proceeds as in the paper.
issues.overall_effect: The self-adjointness theorem and, through it, the realness of the spectrum and the orthogonal eigenbasis on which the β > 0 T-operator (eq:ToperatorBeta) and thm:added-2 rest are unestablished; the nematic analysis covers at most constant directors in 2-D, not the advertised general nematic Helmholtz–Korteweg equation.
issues.title: Self-adjointness of the nematic eigenproblem proved only for constant planar directors
issues.why_classification: A contained repair exists: state the missing hypothesis (and dimension restriction), under which the given integration-by-parts argument is valid; no fundamentally new construction is required, though the advertised generality of the director field is lost.
